question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹540. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 10% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A 10% profit means the Selling Price is 110% of the Cost Price.

SP = 110% of 540

SP = 1.1 × 540 = 594

**∴ The correct answer is ₹594.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹540

Profit = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

 
 CP = ₹540
 
 SP = ?
 

 

 +10% Profit
 + ₹54

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = (10 ÷ 100) × 540

⇒ Profit = ₹54

⇒ SP = 540 + 54

⇒ SP = ₹594

**∴ The correct answer is ₹594.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Selling Price is also calculated from Marked Price (MP) using the rule: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Loss Percentage Formula

When an article is sold at a loss, the Selling Price becomes: SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit

If an article passes through two sellers making profits P₁% and P₂%, the final SP = CP × (1 + P₁/100) × (1 + P₂/100).
